summary: Added validated external FP8 KV-scale loading to the real Qwen3.5 dense/MoE causal classes and delegation from both conditional-generation wrappers. The loader maps nested text model types to their public calibration model types, retains schema and TP-rank validation, skips SSM and pipeline-placeholder layers, and initializes tensor and Python-float scale representations consumed by Triton.

tests.what_was_measured: Dense and MoE causal classes, both conditional wrappers, rank-dependent selection, hybrid layer filtering, all four scale representations, external model-type validation, missing/malformed calibration, and the Triton descale consumer; 5 tests and 6 subtests passed.
Focused regression plus existing Qwen3.5 pipeline-parallel coverage; 10 tests and 6 subtests passed. Raw output: reports/j-25a3b89d4e8d/unit-tests.log.

tests.what_was_measured: The recorded base lacks the Qwen3.5 loader/downstream helper and fails test collection. Raw output: reports/j-25a3b89d4e8d/failing-before.log.

tests.command: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 pinned Python FP8 quantize/dequantize comparison on ROCm
tests.what_was_measured: MI355X gfx950 FP8 E4M3 quantize/dequantize output exactly matched an independently computed CPU reference for scale 0.5. Raw output: reports/j-25a3b89d4e8d/amd-fp8-numerical.log.
Repository formatting, ruff, isort, schema, security, and registered-test checks all passed.

gpu_evidence: One AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 / HIP 7.2.26015, produced an exact FP8 numerical match; see reports/j-25a3b89d4e8d/amd-fp8-numerical.log.
remaining_limitations: The exact reported Qwen3.5-122B-A10B deployment on eight NVIDIA L20 GPUs with TP=8 was unavailable and remains unverified.
No model weights were available, so full server startup and semantic model output were not claimed.
AMD validation covered supported gfx950 FP8 execution and the model-loading/downstream-consumer unit path, not a distributed Qwen3.5 workload.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
